title: Something Is Here
subtitle: The Star Door Mystery
author: Maria & Matthew Smith
stage: Early Years / Foundation, ages 3–5, shared reading
series_position: Book 1, the opening Star Rooms adventure
medium_contract: A continuous read-aloud picture story. Activities need only the book, a finger and an adult's voice. Optional household play and game codes are never prerequisites.
learning_outcomes: Describe what is inside a box before and after the teddy moves.
Notice that the bell remains when its ringing stops.
Distinguish a blank card from a marked card without treating either as absent.
Recall where a teddy was placed before a curtain hid it.
Distinguish no card on a shelf from no shelf.
Use empty, quiet, blank and hidden after experiencing their meanings.

visual_contract.text: Sentence case; all reading and activity instructions above the related picture. Object labels on reveal pages, above the object. Page number in a clear margin.
visual_contract.objects: Reuse the local OpenMoji note, teddy, bell, card, pencil, star and parcel assets. Never generate variants of repeated learning objects. Show box interiors with one consistent open-box diagram, not a sealed parcel icon.
visual_contract.stars: The note includes one map with five outlined stars. Before a discovery its star is hollow. After the visible discovery exactly one further star fills. Reuse that same map throughout; no floating unearned stars.
visual_contract.answers: A question on an even-numbered page is answered after turning the page, unless the activity explicitly asks the reader to compare visible states. Do not put answer labels on question choices.
visual_contract.characters: Mia, Sol and Tavi throughout. Nori joins on page 13, accompanies the remaining discoveries and says goodbye in the library. Poses must depict the action, not merely repeat a scene plate.
visual_contract.continuity: Five places lie along one returning route: box rug, bell room, paper table, curtain nook, shelves by the original Star Door. The map introduced with the note is filed in the library. The delivery ramp is shown before the parcel arrives.

pages.text: Something Is Here
pages.alt: Mia, Sol and Tavi peer towards a closed magical door. A small note peeks through its letter box. No clue stars have been earned.

pages.text: A story to share
pages.subtext:
By Maria & Matthew Smith
Book 1 · Ages 3–5
Read, point, remember and play together.
You do not need the game to enjoy this book.
pages.alt: A note, a teddy and a bell sit apart on a clear page.
pages.production_note: Add edition, text/art licences and attribution in the adult imprint. This manuscript is not a completed edition.

pages.text:
Mia loved finding things.
Today, she was looking for a new adventure.
A little blue door stood open. Mia peeked inside.
pages.alt: Mia leans through an open blue entrance into the warm tower; her feet remain on the outside step. Sol and Tavi can be glimpsed inside.

pages.text:
“Hello! I'm Sol,” said a golden friend.
“I'm Tavi,” said a blue one.
“I'm Mia. Can I come and play?”
pages.alt: Sol waves, Tavi welcomes Mia with an open hand, and Mia smiles back. Each name is printed above its character.

pages.text:
“Yes! Let's try the Star Door,” said Sol.
The friends walked across the room.
The big door was shut.
pages.alt: The trio walk from the little blue entrance towards the different, closed Star Door. Its letter box is clearly visible; no unexplained reward display.

pages.text:
A note slid through the letter box.
It landed beside Mia's feet.
Can you spot the little sheet of paper?
pages.alt: The OpenMoji note lies on the floor beneath the letter box, near Mia's feet. A book and a map on a low table provide distinct, uncrowded alternatives. No answer label.

activity.adult_prompt: A note is a short message written on paper. Which picture looks like that?
activity.answer: The sheet with writing and a pencil, below the letter box. A gesture is sufficient.

pages.text:
“Here it is!” Mia picked up the note.
“There's a message. And a little map!”
Sol and Tavi came closer to listen.
pages.alt: The note is beside Mia's hand in an enlarged, clear view, labelled Note above it. Its reverse shows a map with a route connecting five pictured places and five hollow stars.
pages.code_location: Small map border, separate from the reading text.

pages.text: Mia read the message aloud:
read_aloud_note: Five stars open the Star Door.
pages.alt: The opened note is large enough to read. Beside the message, its map shows box, bell, card, curtain and shelves in route order, ending back at the Star Door. All five stars are hollow.
pages.production_note: The message is sentence case, with the note text above the map. Do not count map icons as earned stars.

pages.text:
“Find nothing? Let's look!” said Sol.
The map led to a box on the rug.
Sol opened the flaps.
pages.alt: Mia, Sol and Tavi gather round the rug. A clearly open cardboard box has its flaps spread; the same teddy emoji is visibly inside, with the near wall in front of its lower body. The map retains five hollow stars.

pages.text:
“My teddy!” said Sol.
He wanted to take it out.
Would the box go away too?
pages.alt: A large open-box diagram makes the teddy visibly inside. There is no second teddy or solved arrow. Space on the rug beside the box is clear.

activity.action: Point to the teddy and box, then make a prediction.
activity.adult_prompt: What do you think will happen to the box?
activity.answer: The box will stay. Accept pointing, naming or a guess; turn the page to compare.

pages.text:
Sol lifted the teddy out.
The box stayed on the rug.
Point inside the box. Now find the teddy.
pages.alt: The identical open-box diagram is shown empty, including its complete interior floor. The same teddy emoji sits fully outside to the right. Labels Box and Teddy sit above the relevant objects.

activity.action: Point into the open interior, then to the teddy outside.
activity.answer: Inside the box is visibly free of toys; the teddy is outside on the rug.

pages.text:
“The box is empty now,” said Tavi.
“No toys inside. But the box is still here!”
Their first star shone.
pages.alt: The empty open-box diagram remains visible, with the same teddy fully outside. The trio's expressions change to pleased discovery. On the map, only the first star is gold; four remain hollow.
pages.code_location: A small printed stamp on the outside of the box, never inside the supposedly empty interior.

pages.text:
“We found a box,” said Mia. “Let's try the bell room.”
They followed the map.
“Hello! I'm Nori. Shall we listen together?”
pages.alt: Nori, wearing a cap, welcomes all three friends into the next room. The map is in Tavi's hand and a clear bell emoji hangs within Nori's reach.

pages.text:
Nori rang the bell. Ding!
Then they waited.
Ask your grown-up to clap once. Listen until the clap stops.
pages.alt: The bell appears once with motion strokes beside it. Nori reaches towards its cord and the three friends listen. No second bell or quiet-state answer is shown.

activity.action: Listen to one clap, then signal when it has stopped.
activity.adult_prompt: Use a gentle clap, not a loud startling sound. If listening is not accessible or comfortable, make a hand-wave together, then stop and notice the hands remain.
activity.answer: The sound or movement stops; the bell or hands remain.

pages.text:
The ringing stopped. The bell stayed.
“Quiet,” said Nori. “The bell isn't ringing now.”
Another star shone. “I'll come with you!”
pages.alt: The same bell hangs still with no motion strokes. Nori points to it, then towards the next doorway. Two map stars are gold and three hollow.
pages.code_location: A small decoration on Nori's cap rim.

pages.text:
The map led them to the paper table.
One card had a mark. One had no marks.
Which card has no marks?
pages.alt: Two identical white-card emojis appear at the same size on the table. One has a single bold blue dot; the other has no mark. Labels do not reveal the answer.

activity.action: Point to the card with no marks.
activity.answer: The unmarked card. A card border is its edge, not a drawn-on mark.

pages.text:
“This one!” Mia pointed.
“A card with no marks is blank.
We can still see the card!”
Their third star shone.
pages.alt: Mia's gesture clearly selects the unmarked card, labelled Blank card above it. The marked card remains beside it for comparison. Three gold stars and two hollow stars appear on the same map.
pages.code_location: On the table edge, not on the blank card.

pages.text:
Draw a tiny shape in the air.
Now stop.
Point to both cards again.
A card can be here with or without a mark.
pages.alt: The same blank and marked cards remain equally visible. Above them are the plain labels No mark and One mark. No imaginary pen mark is added to the blank card.

activity.action: Air-draw, stop, and find both cards.
activity.adult_prompt: Optional: use your own two sheets of paper and make one mark on one. Do not require the child to mark the book.
activity.answer: Both cards remain present. Optional marks can be any shape; there is no art-quality judgement.

pages.text:
Next came a little stage with a curtain.
Sol put his teddy on the stool.
“Let's play a hiding game!”
pages.alt: The curtain is fully open, revealing one stool and the same teddy emoji on it. Sol has placed the teddy there deliberately; no bag, falling toy or unexplained prints. All four friends remain present.

pages.text:
Tavi pulled the curtain shut.
Now they couldn't see the teddy.
Did the teddy leave, or is it behind the curtain?
pages.alt: The same stage, stool position and floor remain. The opaque closed curtain completely hides teddy and stool. Tavi holds the curtain edge. No visible teddy copy, silhouette or answer label.

activity.action: Remember where Sol put the teddy and make a prediction.
activity.adult_prompt: If needed, look back at page 19 together. Do not demand unaided recall.
activity.answer: Behind the curtain; page 22 reveals the same teddy on the stool.

pages.text:
Point to where you think the teddy is.
Shall we peek?
Turn the page slowly...
pages.alt: The curtain stays fully closed. Mia and Nori wait while Sol reaches towards its edge. No teddy or solved trail appears.

activity.action: Point, predict, then enjoy a slow page-turn reveal.
activity.answer: The next page reveals the teddy at the location shown before it was hidden.

pages.text:
There it was, on the stool!
“Hidden,” said Mia. “We couldn't see it, but it hadn't gone.”
Their fourth star shone.
pages.alt: Sol draws the curtain aside to show the same teddy on the same stool, clearly labelled Teddy above it. Four map stars shine; one remains hollow. No hidden teddy label on the now-visible toy.
pages.code_location: Small stitched letters near the outer curtain hem.

pages.text:
Nori checked the map. “One place left!”
They walked back to the Star Door.
Beside it were two shelves. One held a card.
pages.alt: The trio and Nori return to the original closed Star Door. Two matching open shelves stand beside it. One plain card emoji is on the left shelf; the right shelf is empty. Four stars remain earned.

pages.text:
Point to the shelf with a card.
Now find the shelf with no card.
Is that shelf still there?
pages.alt: Two large matching shelves make the comparison unambiguous. The left has one card and the right has none; both shelves have visible sides, top and base. No answer tick or label.

activity.action: Point to each shelf, then to the wood around the empty one.
activity.answer: Yes. No card on that shelf does not mean no shelf.

pages.text:
“Yes!” said Sol. “No card on this shelf.
But here's the shelf!”
The last star shone.
The Star Door began to open.
pages.alt: Sol points unmistakably to the right shelf itself. All five map stars are now gold. Behind the friends, the original Star Door is visibly opening.
pages.code_location: On the map's return path beside the drawn Star Door, not as a main reading instruction.

pages.text:
Beyond the door was a cosy library.
“You did it!” said Nori.
“Let's remember what we found.”
They sat down together.
pages.alt: The open door connects the shelf room to a warm library. All four friends sit together with the five-star map. No repeated image of the original shut door.

pages.text:
Tell Nori a clue!
Which picture shows empty?
Which shows blank?
Point to one. Tell us what is still there.
pages.alt: A clear empty open box and the plain card appear as large unlabelled choices, with a bell as a third distinct choice. No solved matching lines, words below images or hidden-object state mistakes.

activity.action: Choose the box for empty or the card for blank; name or point to the thing that remains.
activity.adult_prompt: Accept either clue. For a further recall question, ask where the teddy was hiding. Look back if needed.
activity.answer: Empty box: box remains. Blank card: card remains. Teddy was on the stool behind the curtain.

pages.text:
An empty box. A blank card.
You found them!
The box was still there. So was the card.
Neither had vanished.
pages.alt: The same choices now have labels above them. The open box interior remains clear. The blank card has no mark, including no code. The bell is removed from this answer composition, not depicted as disappearing in the story.

pages.text:
We didn't find a thing called nothing.
We found things that were empty, quiet, blank or hidden.
These words help us tell someone what we mean.
pages.alt: Four small but legible reminder pictures: empty open box; still bell; unmarked card; closed curtain. Each word sits above its picture. Do not show a visible teddy labelled hidden.
pages.adult_boundary: The story introduces the SFT distinction about nothing through limited everyday observations. It is not a proof of a universal empirical claim, nor a reason to ban the everyday word nothing.

pages.text:
Try it with me!
If a toy is behind a curtain, say,
“My toy is hidden.”
Now your friend knows where to look.
pages.alt: A simple remembered scene shows a closed curtain and Mia pointing towards it, without exposing the hidden teddy. The narrator's direct speech is above the picture.

pages.text:
Mia put their map in the library stand.
“Come back soon!” said Nori.
A little hatch opened high on the wall.
A ramp ran down to the rug.
pages.alt: Mia places the same five-star map in a clearly visible stand; Nori waves goodbye at the doorway. A newly open delivery hatch connects to an uninterrupted ramp ending at the rug. No parcel has arrived yet.

pages.text:
Whoosh! A parcel slid down the ramp.
Its label said, “For Mia, Sol and Tavi.”
“What's inside?” said Sol.
Their next adventure was waiting.
pages.alt: The same ramp now ends beside one sealed parcel emoji on the rug. Its addressee label is legible above it. The main trio gather around it; Nori has left. This parcel is distinct from the earlier open toy box.

remaining_work: Complete purpose-drawn character action illustrations and precise teaching diagrams.
Render and inspect all 32 pages; only a four-page box sequence is currently being developed as the first layout proof.
Create the matching accessible and adult editions from this source.
Synchronise revised book/game star order and narration before labelling the pair review-ready.
Confirm and test optional code behavior; the existing game strings are not a finished early-concept unlock.
